Comment BENCE JONES PROTEIN ABSENT IN URINE

 
The presence of a Bence Jones protein is characterized by :

  • A monoclonal band detected with one of the anti-free and bound light chains or lambda antisera(K or L tracks)
  • The same monoclonal band detected with the corresponding anti-free light chain antiserum. (KF or LF)
  • No reaction with the trivalent antiserum(GAM track)

Serum paraprotein eliminated in urine without a Bence Jones protein is characterized by

  • One monoclonal band was detected with the trivalent antiserum.
  • The same band detected with one of the anti-free and bound light chain antisera and
  • No reaction with the corresponding anti-free light chain antiserum

Serum paraprotein eliminated in urine with a Bence Jones protein is characterized by

  • One monoclonal band detected with the trivalent antiserum
  • The same band detected with one of the anti-free and bound light chain antisera
  • One monoclonal band was detected with one of the anti-free and bound light chain antisera. This band generally does not migrate at the same level as one detected with the trivalent antiserum.
  • The same band was detected with one of the anti-free light chain antisera.
  • In rare cases, the two bands migrate together (then, the staining in the light chain track is stronger than that in the GAM track)

Polymerized forms of Bence Jones Protein are characterized by

  • Lack of reaction with the trivalent antiserum.
  • Several bands revealed with one of the anti-free and bound light chain Antisera.
  • The same bands may also be detected with the corresponding free light chain Antiserum.

COMMENTS: BAND SEEN IN ALBUMIN, ALPHA 1, ALPHA 2 & BETA REGION.

Interpretation :

  • It allows detection by densitometry scanning & yielding relative concentration (Percentage) of individual protein zone and monoclonal components which must be confirmed & identified by immunofixation and the detection of proteins of tubular, glomerular or mixed origin which must be confirmed by appropriate tests.
  • Urine electrophoresis on samples with urinary total proteins less than 300 mg/day often does not yield different band formation for various protein fractions. For such samples advised further workup and correlation with urinary albumin quantification. These samples are retested using concentration method – after pretreatment with fast ultrafiltration using centrifugal filter devices, resulting in 80 fold concentration of urine samples
